scope_choices: This is automated API model review. The current response is a skeptical second model pass over supplied primary text and prior automated page-review notes, not independent human verification or replication.
All 21 text pages were supplied and read. Original page images were not attached in this synthesis call; visual descriptions and coverage rely on the supplied per-page image-review notes.
The source hash, local path and availability are supplied registry information, not independently recomputed or checked against a filesystem.
The supplied ontology packet omits the full operational feature catalogue. Feature assertions are intentionally empty as requested; no claim of completed 128-feature annotation is made.
No executable JSON Schema validator, graph build, repository access, dataset retrieval, code execution or independent scientific validation was performed in this response.

The method is explicitly static image classification. Persistent health-world state, learned temporal transitions, specified-action future prediction, matched intervention alternatives and model-coupled planning are not implemented in the described evaluated pipeline.
Conversational turns, capture instructions, training epochs, architectural depth, saliency maps and prospective feature plans do not establish world-model capability.
Public dataset image counts are not patient counts. Unique patients, institutions, demographics, inclusion criteria and early-stage case distribution are not reported.
The datasets lack expert-verified ground truth and oncologist-confirmed diagnoses. Actual pathology correspondence is expressly uncertain.

Reported public oral-photograph holdout testing supports only a narrowly scoped R2 facet. It does not establish reliable clinical labels, patient-independent validation, external validation or end-to-end chatbot effectiveness.
Final post-deduplication counts, split counts, stratification, random seeds, patient/lesion separation and overlap across public resources are unresolved.
RMS-based duplicate removal is described but its scale, formula details, crop/transformation robustness and number removed are not reported.
The effects of blur, resizing and border handling on subtle pathological features were not adequately evaluated; authors acknowledge possible suppression of clinically relevant information.
The datasets do not represent population screening prevalence, early-stage presentations or the full variability of clinical and patient-generated images.

Hyperparameter tuning is asserted, but Table 3 supplies one common configuration without search ranges, trial counts, selection results, optimizer, complete network definitions or checkpoint-selection rules.
Pretrained initialization, retained trainable layers, parameter counts, weights and an executable environment manifest are not reported.
Python 3.13.7 and Matplotlib 1.5.x are reported alongside TensorFlow/Keras 2.9; a compatible reproducible environment is not established.
Metric values and intervals are preserved as printed. Repeated-run/fold design, test denominators, confidence-interval construction and Table 4 parenthesized quantities are insufficiently explained.

Several reported accuracy values are incompatible with corresponding sensitivity/specificity values under a common conventional binary confusion matrix; differing aggregation could matter but is not documented.
DenseNet121 DOR is 2.58 in Table 4 and Figure 7, while its printed 95% interval is (2.68, 3.08). Neither value was silently corrected.

Narrative rankings of DenseNet201 accuracy and CNN/DenseNet agreement do not match the tables. The blanket narrowest-confidence-interval claim for InceptionV3 is also unsupported by the displayed intervals.
Table 2 labels loss as a percentage without defining the loss function or scaling. Loss was not converted to percentages.
Metric confidence intervals do not establish predictive probability calibration. Displayed classifier scores are not prevalence-adjusted patient cancer risks.
CAM outputs are illustrated but localization accuracy, explanation faithfulness, causal attribution and effects on user understanding or trust are not evaluated.
The workflow depicts symptom-image fusion, but the limitations explicitly say the evaluated model excludes symptom narratives and patient histories.
The implemented NLP model, prompts, conversational memory, multilingual handling, risk thresholds and symptom-fusion algorithm are not specified sufficiently.
Spanish Telegram operation is described in methods; broader multilingual web/mobile claims lack separate platform/language validation.

Methods describe interviews and usability/alpha/beta testing, while limitations deny usability, user-experience and acceptability evaluations. No participant counts, defined human-study outcomes or sufficient R4 evidence resolve the conflict.
Latency, memory and energy consumption were explicitly not measured. Real-time, low-latency, lightweight and edge-deployment claims are not demonstrated by CPU executability.
The chatbot was not tested live clinically or with clinician oversight. Prospective silent use, patient feasibility and comparative effectiveness are not established.
The authors explicitly consider the current models unsuitable for decision support despite favorable screening and clinical-integration language elsewhere.
No reduction in diagnostic delay, mortality, anxiety, unnecessary interventions, inequity or resource use, and no improvement in health literacy or engagement, was measured.
Clinical acceptance thresholds, screening negative predictive value and a validated operating point are not reported; no threshold was invented.
Non-diagnostic messaging and consultation recommendations do not establish evaluated abstention, a hard safety guard, actual human escalation or protection against automation bias.
GDPR compliance, secure storage, encryption and security testing are asserted without sufficient configuration, threat model, audit or effectiveness evidence. Ethics/IRB approval is not reported.
Federated learning, local inference, EHR integration, structured image-capture validation, longitudinal tracking and clinical/user studies are future work, not implemented capabilities.
Generic TRL2 is author-stated with a general TRL citation; it is not an independently assessed MLTRL level, clinical authorization or R0/R1/R2 equivalence.
Code availability wording mixes a future release promise with a present repository-accessibility statement. Repository availability, completeness, license and weights were not checked.
The article's CC BY license cannot be transferred automatically to code, datasets or model weights.
References and publisher material on pages 19–21 were read as supplied. Cited publications and dataset links were not independently retrieved, and their capabilities were not inherited.
Potential citation-support mismatches, including broad NLP/healthcare citations and a citrus-classification reference for Inception-v3, require source verification rather than assumptions.
BP_COMPONENT denotes limited architectural relevance for encoders, interfaces and risk communication. It does not reverse the static-prediction exclusion or imply a verified world model.
No separate StudyLineage overlap was established from other primary papers; absence of a discovered overlap is not proof of independence.
